title: Patch: a daily game's board never goes backwards: a read already under way cannot overwrite the answer to the move the player just made
thread:
**Issue #4846 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4846: Patch: a daily game's board never goes backwards: a read already under way cannot overwrite the answer to the move the player just made
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

On a daily game's board (`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx`), a read that was already out when the player acted can land after the action's answer and put the older state back on screen.

1. A read goes out (`:131-153`). `pollWhileVisible` (`apps/web/src/game/net.ts:158-189`) reads at once when the tab shows again, or on the first input after `IDLE_QUIET_MS` (ten minutes), and input includes `pointermove` and `keydown`. So a player coming back to a daily board fires `GET /api/daily/games/:id` just before they move.
2. The player acts. `send` (`:174-219`) posts the action with `after: shown.seq`. Nothing cancels the read in flight: the `!sending.current` guard at `:169` only stops a read from *starting* during a send.
3. The POST's answer (seq N+1) lands and `setGame(answer)` runs.
4. The earlier GET, which the server read at seq N, lands afterwards. Its `canceled` flag flips only when `reads` is bumped or the board unmounts, so `setGame(answer)` runs again with the older state.

The player sees their move undone: the card back in hand, or their turn back after End turn, or a conceded game live again, with the old list of legal moves. The next action goes `after: N` and gets 409 `stale`, which rereads silently; otherwise the 60-second poll puts it right.

By reading, with high confidence in the code path. How often it fires depends on the order of two responses; the first GET after a long idle is the slow one (the server may be waking), and the player's first move races it.

### What should happen

The board never goes backwards. `DailyGame.seq` (`apps/web/src/net/daily.ts:74-75`: "The last action's number: the next action is sent `after` it") is there to order answers, and the file's header says "the board draws the answer". Every answer carries `seq`; the board never compares it.

### How to reproduce

A test in `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` with its fake API (it has about thirty tests and none of an older read after a newer answer):

1. Mount the board at seq 5 with `hasMove`.
2. Trigger a reread whose promise is held.
3. Send End turn and resolve its POST with seq 6 and `hasMove: false`.
4. Resolve the held GET with seq 5.
5. Assert the board still shows seq 6 with End turn unlit. Today it shows seq 5 with End turn lit again.

### Where

The client: `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx` (the read effect, the poll and `send`).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- In the read effect, ignore an answer whose `seq` is below the shown game's `seq` for the same `matchId`. Or bump a generation in `send`, so a read already out is dropped when it lands. The first is the smaller change and also covers two reads landing out of order.
- An `expired` answer (R3934000) has no `seq`; decide how it orders against a live answer and say so in the test.
- Overlapping reads already cancel each other; only read against send is unguarded. `sharedGet`'s de-duplication (`apps/web/src/net/api.ts:225`) does not help here, because a POST without an idempotency key does not move the write epoch.
- The server already refuses a stale action (`409 stale`), so nothing wrong is ever written: this is what the player sees for up to a minute.
- Run with `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`.

Found by an audit of the web client's network layer, by reading (the client's tests could not be run where the audit ran).

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/45577550173)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

A daily game's board never draws an answer older than what it already shows. A `GET /api/daily/games/:id` that was already out when the player acted and lands after the action's answer is dropped by comparing `DailyGame.seq`, so the player never sees their move undone (card back in hand, turn back, conceded game live again) and the next action never spurious-409s `stale`. An `expired` answer (R3934000, no `seq`) always replaces a live board. One new board test proves the race; no server, spec, or config change.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx` | change | Read effect's answer branch (`useEffect` on `[matchId, reads]`, ~:131-153): seq guard + ordering comment; one sentence in the file header comment |
| `apps/web/src/test/stubServer.ts` | change | `Handler` type and the stubbed `fetch`: a handler may return `Promise<Reply>` so a test can hold a request |
| `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` | change | New `describe("#4846 …")` with one `it("#4846 …")` staging the issue's repro, plus the expired-ordering decision stated in a comment |

Must not touch: anything under `crates/`, `apps/edge`, `apps/admin`, `e2e`, `spec/` (no ruling note, no `spec/pending/4846.md` — see below), `apps/web/src/wire/`, `apps/web` configs, or `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`. No new constant is needed (CLAUDE.md rule 9: the ordering key is the existing `seq`).

Governing spec: §9.13 (actions name their `after` seq, stale refused; purge answers `expired`), R3840000 (when the board rereads — unchanged), R3934000 (`expired` replaces the board), R3206000 (concurrent same-path reads join). No new ruling: `seq` ordering is already specified and this is presentation-only (rule 7); precedent #3841 fixed client send-ordering the same way with `#issue`-named tests. R3840000's note once rejected exactly this guard as rarely needed; this issue reverses that call on new evidence (the idle-wake race), but its rule paragraph still holds, so the note is left alone.

## Steps

1. **`apps/web/src/test/stubServer.ts`: allow a handler to hold a request.** Change `export type Handler = (call: Call) => Reply | undefined;` to `(call: Call) => Reply | Promise<Reply> | undefined;`. Change the stubbed fetch from `vi.fn((input, init) => { …; return Promise.resolve(jsonResponse(…)); })` to an `async` function that does `const reply = (await handler(call)) ?? refusal(404, "not_found", …); return jsonResponse(reply.status, reply.body);`. Add one line to the file's header comment: a handler may return a promise to hold a request until the test releases it. Nothing else in the file changes; every existing handler still returns a plain `Reply`.
2. **`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`: add the repro test (red).** Insert before `describe("R4621000 …")` a new block `describe("#4846 the board never goes backwards", …)` with one test `it("#4846 a read already out when End turn is sent lands after its answer and is dropped", …)`. It calls `stubServer` directly (`Reply` is already imported) with a counter `gets`:
   - `GET /api/daily/games/g-1`: first call answers `{ status: 200, body: dailyGame({ seq: 5 }) }` at once (default fixture: `hasMove: true`, legal `[END_TURN, CONCEDE]`); later calls return `new Promise<Reply>((resolve) => { releaseReread = resolve; })` with `let releaseReread: ((reply: Reply) => void) | null = null;` declared above.
   - `POST /api/daily/games/g-1/actions` answers `{ status: 200, body: dailyGame({ seq: 6, hasMove: false, legal: [CONCEDE], view: baseView({ active: "p2" }), holds: [] }) }` at once; anything else returns `undefined` (the stub's 404 default).
   - Render `<DailyBoard matchId="g-1" />`; `await screen.findByTestId("end-turn", undefined, SLOW)`; assert enabled.
   - Fire the held reread: `act(() => { setVisibility("hidden"); }); act(() => { setVisibility("visible"); });` (copies the R3840000 pattern; `setVisibility` is already imported). Then `await waitFor(() => { expect(server.to("GET", GAME)).toHaveLength(2); }, SLOW)` with `const GAME = "/api/daily/games/g-1"`.
   - `fireEvent.click(screen.getByTestId("end-turn"))`; `await waitFor(() => { expect(screen.getByTestId(dailyTestid.board)).toHaveAttribute("data-has-move", "false"); }, SLOW)`; assert `screen.getByTestId("end-turn")` `toBeDisabled()` with text `Enemy turn`; assert the POST body is `{ after: 5, action: END_TURN }` with a non-empty string nonce (copies the `#3727 End turn…` assertions).
   - `expect(releaseReread).not.toBeNull();` (never let this test pass vacuously), then `await act(async () => { releaseReread?.({ status: 200, body: dailyGame({ seq: 5 }) }); }); await flush();`.
   - Assert the board still shows seq 6: `data-has-move` is `"false"`, `end-turn` is still disabled, and `server.to("GET", GAME)` still has length 2 (no reread fired).
   - Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` and watch this test fail (today the stale seq-5 answer redraws End turn lit).
3. **`apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx`: drop older answers (green).** In the read effect, replace the answer branch with:
   - `if (canceled) return;` stays first.
   - If `"expired" in answer`: `setExpired(answer); setGame(null);` (unchanged behavior).
   - Else: `const shown = current.current; if (shown !== null && shown.matchId === answer.matchId && answer.seq < shown.seq) return;` then `setGame(answer); setExpired(null);`.
   - `setLoadError(null);` stays last (a dropped answer returns before it).
   - Above the branch put this comment: every live answer carries the log row it was read at (`DailyGame.seq`, which the next action is sent `after`), so a live answer below the shown game's `seq` is a read that was already out when a newer answer landed, and is dropped; an equal one still applies, so a reread refreshes the clock. An `expired` answer carries no `seq` and always applies: the purge only moves forward, so it is newer than any live board of this game. A live answer can never land after one did — same-path reads join while one is out (R3206000), and once the game is gone the poll, the social read and `send` all stop reading — so the live branch needs no expired check.
   - Extend the header sentence ending "and the board draws the answer." with: "A read already out when the player acts may land after the action's answer; the board drops any answer below the shown game's `seq`, so it never goes backwards (#4846)."
   - Do not touch `send`, the poll, `sharedGet`, or any other file. Re-run the test file: all green.
4. **Prove nothing else broke.** Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` (the `Handler` change is shared test infra — typecheck covers every consumer), and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.tsx apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx apps/web/src/test/stubServer.ts`.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`, new `describe("#4846 the board never goes backwards")`:
  - `it("#4846 a read already out when End turn is sent lands after its answer and is dropped")`: mounts at seq 5 with the move, holds a reread, sends End turn (POST answered seq 6, move gone), resolves the held GET with seq 5, asserts the board still shows seq 6 (`data-has-move="false"`, End turn disabled reading "Enemy turn") with no further GET. Fails before step 3, passes after. The test's closing comment states the expired decision: `expired` always replaces a live board; the reverse needs no test because a live answer cannot land after a shown `expired` (reads join per R3206000; nothing reads once the game is null).
- No other test files change. Existing coverage relied on: `#3727 End turn…` (POST `after`/nonce shape), the R3840000 block (visibility-triggered rereads, ended-game polling), and the R3934000 block (live→expired transition, expired panel, no reads after).
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx`; `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`.

## Done when

- [ ] A held GET resolving with seq 5 after a seq-6 POST answer leaves the board at seq 6 (End turn unlit), per the new test.
- [ ] Equal-seq rereads still apply (clock refresh preserved by the strict `<`).
- [ ] `expired` still replaces a live board and reads stop after (existing R3934000 tests green).
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/daily/DailyBoard.test.tsx` green, including a red-before/green-after run of the new test.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and eslint on the three touched files clean.
- [ ] Diff touches exactly the three files above; no spec, server, or generated files.

## Risks

- The async `stubServer` fetch adds a microtask before answers resolve. Every consumer already awaits via `findBy`/`waitFor`/`flush`; typecheck plus the DailyBoard file prove it, but a flaky neighbor would show in CI's web job, not here.
- Two reads landing out of order through the real stack cannot be staged in a test (same-path GETs join in `sharedGet`; superseded effect reads cancel), so only the read-vs-send race has a test; the guard covers the read-vs-read case by construction.
- The `shown.matchId === answer.matchId` check never fires today (effect cleanup cancels old-matchId answers); it is belt-and-braces for the issue's "for the same matchId".
- If the reviewer wants R3840000's rejected-rationale sentence updated or a ruling note after all, that is a one-paragraph follow-up on the issue, not part of this build.

## Open questions

None. The expired-ordering decision the task left open is settled above (expired always wins; live-after-expired is impossible through this stack, so no ref and no second test), with the rejected alternative recorded.
```
